title: Wavefront attention hyperfusion kernel and async-KV conductor for continuous batching
author: Luca Martinez
description:
Motivation: tail latency and throughput for mixed sequence-length traffic remain the top cost drivers for our hosted workloads. This PR introduces a new attention microkernel (Wavefront Hyperfusion) plus an async-KV conductor that together improve single-request latency and steady-state throughput under continuous batching.

What I changed (high level):
- Implemented Wavefront Hyperfusion kernel (CUDA) that fuses softmax, rotary/rope application, and QK reduction with a single memory pass and tiled wavefront scheduling tuned for 16/32/64 heads.
- Added async-KV conductor component in the runtime scheduler that performs background KV materialization, eviction hints, and non-blocking prefix cache fills to reduce KV stall time for streaming workloads.
- Scheduler integration: new micro-batching policy (wavefront-aware) and adaptive spill thresholds that let the conductor prefetch for low-latency SLOs.
- Added SIMD-friendly rearrange and a small fp16 accumulation path with overflow checks.
- Tests, microbench harnesses, and perf dashboards updated.

Why this is different: previous Flash/bridge approaches required multiple memory passes or per-layer reshapes. Wavefront Hyperfusion minimizes global memory traffic and aligns with our continuous batching pipeline by producing KV-ready fragments that the conductor can consume asynchronously.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation with unit tests
- [x] Scheduler hooks and end-to-end regression tests
- [x] Performance microbench suite added
- [x] Docs: runtime/attn/README and release notes
- [x] Backwards-compatible on-model-API (no changes to public SDK)

How to validate locally: run tests/runtime/attn_wavefront_microbench.sh and the end-to-end perf replay in tests/perf/continuous_batching_replay.py with --model gpt-small --seq 64/128. Repro script included in PR.

Notes: Fusion has been gated behind runtime flag RW_ENABLE_WAVEFRONT (default off on canaries). We will progressively enable on dedicated fleets after a 2-week canary window.

Risks: fp16 accumulation requires observed validation; overflow detection added but we keep an fp32 fallback path. KV prefetching increases background bandwidth; conductor uses tenant-aware throttles to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
